_readme: Verified 'these different NAMES are one company' facts.
insurer_key() in canonicalize_financials.py collapses TYPOGRAPHIC variants only
- case, '&' vs 'and', 'Co. Ltd.' vs 'Ltd', punctuation. It deliberately does not
strip distinguishing words, because doing so would fuse separately licensed
entities of one group: Bajaj Allianz Life and Bajaj Allianz General are two
That leaves a gap no string function can close. When the handbook renders one
company under two genuinely different names, only a real-world fact can merge
them. This file is where those facts live, so the default stays conservative and
every merge is explicit, reviewable and attributable.
Add an entry ONLY after confirming the companies are the same legal entity.
A wrong entry here silently fuses two real insurers into one, which is far
harder to notice than the split it fixes.
'canonical' is pinned as the display name - it overrides the usual
longest-variant heuristic, which would otherwise have picked the wrong Galaxy
name simply because it is longer.

variants: Galaxy Health and Allied Insurance Ltd.
why: One SAHI insurer appearing under two names in different tables of
same source workbook, and ZERO overlapping (metric, line-of-business,
year) triples - the two names carry complementary halves of one book,
not duplicate filings. 'Galaxy Health and Allied Insurance Ltd.' held
8 lines of business (Health, Balance Sheet, Investments, Claims);
'Galaxy Health Insurance Co. Ltd' held Personal Accident alone,
stranding 6,390 policies and 274 lakh of gross premium off the profile.
Confirmed as the same company by the user on 2026-07-30, who also
chose the 'Co. Ltd' rendering as canonical.
